Oh boy, where do I even start? After 8 years as an auto insurance agent, I have zero loyalty left to protect these companies.

The "File and Use" Scam Here's something most people don't know: in many states, insurance companies can raise your rates immediately and justify it later. We'd implement 15-20% increases across entire ZIP codes, knowing regulators would take months to review. By then, we'd collected millions in extra premiums.

Claim Frequency Was Irrelevant Your rates weren't really based on how often you'd claim - they were based on how likely you were to shop around. A customer with 3 claims who got quotes every year paid less than a claim-free customer who never compared rates. It was pure price discrimination.

As a student in her early twenties, I would never think of Georgia as a potential destination for traveling if not for my college's winter study program. My preconception was that Tbilisi is perhaps not worth my time as compared to some other fancy cities such as London or Paris or Berlin. But as it turned out, Tbilisi is now one of my favorite places on earth.

While I am in Tbilisi, I got the chance to intern at the Tbilisi State Conservatoire. The experience was just amazing! I got to see ensemble rehearsals led by my talented manager, and even collaborated with him for a flute piece in Carmen. I was also shown around the library, where ancient manuscripts were piled up in an old way that brings back nostalgia, where books from the 5th century were waiting to be digitized for the benefit of all mankind. There was also this history museum within the conservatoire housing exhibitions from musicians of the 18-19 century. Most of these musicians played an influential role on the development of classical music. I even got to play on Sergei Rachmaninoff's personal instrument! (He's my favorite composer ever!!!) I also invited all my friends on my trip to join me at a folk music concert held at the conservatoire. We all loved it and learned a lot about Georgia's national character through the beautiful voices.

Apart from its vibrant music scenes and cultural splendor, Tbilisi boasts the most friendly people and delicious cuisine. My host family was super lovely! I arrived here on my birthday and they celebrated it with me though I did not even expect them to know! And on Jan.7th (the Georgian Xmas) we had guests over and they dressed up as Santas and gave us candies! :) Celebrations went on for hours into the night and of course - accompanied with great wine and cheerful laughter! For food, anyone here should try Hingali. It is surprisingly similar to China's steamed buns (包子). I heard it was probably because of the Mongols' influence. Very yummy! In terms of drinks, Georgian wine is amazing. I can't really comment much on the taste because I'm not a habitual wine drinker, but based on what I heard, the wine here is top-class! I was surprised at the endless amount of food that Georgian families put on the table to treat their guests. They call this "feasts" - literally though! Having been here only for a short time, I already find Georgian people's hospitality inviting and sometimes overwhelming (in the most positive way of course)!

![](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-1cd650efd8d97d5a678dcc434a11e4cd-lq)

(Local people, from an excursion)

* * *

Tbilisi is a city whose natural beauty and history are often underrated among myriad fabulous cities of this world. I remember that a friend on my trip saying that whenever she revisits a city after a period of time, it would undergo dramatic changes that catch her off guard. But she feels like no matter how many years elapse, the spirit of Tbilisi will stay the same. Tbilisi (or broadly speaking, Georgia) is totally worth your time if you're an adventurous soul craving for something novel, something different from the highly commercialized western society, and surprising discoveries of humanity that will bring tears to your eyes.

P.S. Remember to make lots of friends. :)

My husband and I spent three incredible days travelling to the stunningly beautiful, Kazbegi, Gudauri, Mtskheta and Kakheti regions with amazing Mukhran and his excellent, super safe, very capable driver, George. The very comfortable, very well maintained, Toyota Prado, was the perfect vehicle for this trip. Mukhran’s English is excellent! We really enjoyed his warm, friendly, relaxed and welcoming personality and we felt as if we had known him forever! His historical, cultural, geographical and political knowledge was excellent! Each day was an amazing learning experience!
